fdi_cap_timeline.event: Insurance opened to private players; foreign equity capped at 26% of paid-up capital
Cap raised from 26% to 49% (Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015; Indian ownership and control retained)
Cap raised from 49% to 74% (Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2021; Union Budget 2021-22 proposal); majority of directors and key managers had to be resident Indians

Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025 passed by Parliament in Dec 2025 (Gazette notification 21 Dec 2025); allows up to 100% foreign investment (FDI plus FPI) in insurers; first announced in Union Budget 2025-26

Act in force from 5 Feb 2026 (Section 25 excluded); DPIIT Press Note 1 (2026 Series) allows 100% FDI in insurers under the automatic route (reported 12 Feb 2026); LIC stays at 20% under the automatic route

industry.current_rules: Up to 100% foreign investment (FDI plus FPI) is allowed in Indian insurers under the automatic route (DPIIT Press Note 1 of 2026) following the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025 (Gazette 21 Dec 2025; most provisions in force 5 Feb 2026). At least one of Chairperson, MD or CEO must be a resident Indian citizen; the earlier majority-resident-directors/KMP rule has been dropped (Vinod Kothari dates the Press Note change to 2 May 2026). LIC's foreign limit stays at 20% (automatic route). No invest-premiums-in-India condition appears in the notified conditions reviewed (the Budget 2025-26 speech had linked 100% to it) - verify against the Press Note text.

fdi_inflows.scope: Cumulative FDI into insurance companies since the cap rose to 49%, per Financial Services Secretary (PTI interview, 18 Mar 2024); Finance Ministry figure, not a DPIIT table
FDI into the insurance sector in the first three months after the cap was raised to 49% (BS/ANI, Aug 2015)
Total foreign investment across the whole insurance sector (life, general, health), as stated by the IRDAI chairman

industry.notes: Foreign share of paid-up equity at 31 Dec 2024 (IRDAI annexure to Lok Sabha Starred Q112, 28 Jul 2025): private life insurers 47.82%, private general 40.80%, standalone health 29.46%; four life insurers at 74% (Ageas Federal, Aviva, CreditAccess Life, Generali Central). Whole life industry incl. LIC: 29.26% in FY24 (IRDAI via Business Standard, 14 Nov 2025). IRDAI foreign share includes FPI holdings in listed insurers. No insurance-specific DPIIT annual series found. 2026 deals: Prudential plc to buy 75% of Bharti Life (announced 17 May 2026, pending); Jio Financial-Allianz 50:50 insurance JV (Deccan Chronicle, 18 May 2026); Republic World (3 Jul 2026) reports IRDAI approved one unnamed insurer's move to 100% foreign ownership and is reviewing another; GoI sold 6.5% of LIC by OFS (Aug 2026).

sbi.notes: Promoter line (55.31%) is the exchange-filing summary and matches SBI alone, so no foreign promoter is shown; a residual BNP Paribas Cardif holding (former JV partner) is not separately confirmed. IRDAI total foreign share was 24.12% at Dec 2024 (FPI plus any residual foreign holding).

hdfc.notes: Promoter line (50.53%) is the exchange-filing summary and matches HDFC Bank alone, so no foreign promoter is shown; abrdn's earlier exit is not separately sourced here. IRDAI total foreign share was 25.30% at Dec 2024 (essentially FPI).

events.text: Government of India sold up to 6.5% of LIC through an OFS (floor price Rs 382, about Rs 31,000 crore), cutting its holding from 96.5% to 90%; FPI holding rose from 0.44% (Jun 2026) to 1.55% (Sep 2026)

lic.notes: Promoter row on the exchange summary is labelled Indian Promoters (Government of India); Other public = 10.00% public holding less mutual funds and FPIs (derived). Foreign investment in LIC stays capped at 20% under the automatic route even though other insurers can have 100%.

events.text: CNBC-TV18 reported Prudential plc was exploring an exit from ICICI Prudential Life, in talks with the Bharti group company (unconfirmed at the time)

Prudential plc agreed (17 May 2026) to buy 75% of Bharti Life; completion requires it to cut its ~22% ICICI Prudential Life holding below 10% and stop being a promoter, on a timeframe to be agreed with regulators; ICICI Pru shares fell ~9%

icici.notes: Bank/Prudential stakes are Mar 2026 (Outlook Business); public split is Sep 2026 (Upstox). The exchange summary shows total promoter holding of 74.70% at Sep 2026, about 1.8 pts above the Mar 2026 ICICI Bank + Prudential sum (72.88%), so ICICI Bank's stake may have risen - verify on NSE/BSE. IRDAI foreign share was 36.91% at Dec 2024 (Prudential plus FPIs).

events.text: Axis Bank announced a plan to buy 29% of Max Life for Rs 1,592 crore to reach 30% (a 70:30 JV with Max Financial Services); its holding is about 20% today
Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance's ~21% direct stake in Max Life was swapped into shares of listed parent Max Financial Services (IRDAI nod Nov 2020), moving its holding up to the parent
Max Life Insurance rebranded Axis Max Life Insurance (13 Dec 2024)
Axis Bank raised its stake to 19.9% (about Rs 380 crore)

axismax.notes: Foreign exposure sits at parent level: Mitsui Sumitomo holds 21.86% of Max Financial Services (Sep 2026, listed under FDI), about 17.5% look-through of the insurer (21.86% x 80%, derived); IRDAI's Dec-2024 foreign-share list does not include Max Life. FPI 48.61%, mutual funds 35.49%, other DII 8.21% and promoters 1.25% (Sep 2026) refer to the listed parent MFSL, not the insurer. Wikipedia infobox shows Axis Bank at 20%. IFC put in Rs 285 crore of subordinated debt in Nov 2025 (not equity).

events.text: Bajaj Finserv agreed to buy Allianz SE's 26% in Bajaj Allianz Life (Rs 10,400 crore) and Bajaj Allianz General (Rs 13,780 crore), total Rs 24,180 crore, lifting its holding from 74% to 100% on closing; CCI and IRDAI approvals pending at announcement
Allianz exit completed after final regulatory approvals; Bajaj Finserv took full ownership of the insurance arms
Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance renamed Bajaj Life Insurance (and Bajaj Allianz General became Bajaj General Insurance), announced early Oct 2025

bajaj.notes: Allianz held 26% until the 2025 buyout (IRDAI Dec 2024 foreign share 26.00%). 100% is per the Mar 2025 deal terms; completion and rename dates from Oct 2025 reports (headlines and URL date), effective date of the new name may be a few weeks later.

events.text: Bharti Life Ventures (Bharti Enterprises) announced it would buy out AXA's 49% stake in Bharti AXA Life, giving Bharti sole control after 17 years of the JV; Bharti was also seeking new strategic or financial partners

Prudential plc agreed (17 May 2026) to buy 75% of Bharti Life from Bharti and four 360 ONE funds for Rs 3,500 crore initial cash plus up to Rs 700 crore if conditions are met; subject to regulatory approvals and to Prudential cutting its ICICI Prudential Life stake below 10%
Bharti AXA Life Insurance now trades as Bharti Life Insurance (new name used in May 2026 reports)

bharti.notes: Current shareholder split (Bharti vs four 360 ONE funds) not found; AXA's 49% is absent from IRDAI's Dec-2024 foreign-share list, so foreign stake is shown as nil. The Prudential 75% deal was still pending approvals in the sources reviewed (no completion found).
